A1.justification: Both complete 41-page PDFs describe SECA, with matching main sections and Appendices A-O. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the text, equations, figures and tables. Pages 7-41 are visually identical.

before.justification: v2 reports original MMLU attack experiments, analyses of generated prompts and hallucinations, and comparisons between human and LLM evaluators in Section 3, with additional results in Appendices M-N.

after.justification: v3 retains the original attack experiments, empirical analyses and evaluator-agreement measurements in Section 3 and Appendices M-N.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, its objective, proposer, feasibility filtering and candidate selection are unchanged. Section 2.2's more explicit instruction-sampling description clarifies the procedure already documented in v2's Appendix G.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same open-ended multiple-choice question-answering task across 16 MMLU subjects. Section 3 and Appendices M-N retain the same dataset and task coverage, without additional domains or test scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains Raw and GCG as SECA's comparators, while Appendices M-N retain comparisons with Raw prompts. The illustrative jailbreak comparisons in Appendix D are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Data filtering, sample sizes, model configurations, attack budgets and evaluation metrics in Section 3.1 and Appendix L are unchanged. Section 3.2 replaces 'constraint violations' with 'semantic errors' while referring to the same SEE/SCE measures.

E4.justification: The convergence, hallucination-type, prompt-diversity and evaluator-agreement analyses in Sections 3.3-3.4 are unchanged, as are the attack examples in Appendices B and K. No ablation or robustness study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard deviations from 10,000 bootstrap samples in Table 2 and Figure 4, and specify seed 42 in Appendix L. Statistical reporting practices and disclosed seed information are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings are retained. For example, Table 2 reports identical Llama-3-3B ASR@30 values: 48.20% for Raw, 80.29% for SECA and 6.26% for GCG. Tables 3 and 8-13 and Figures 3-4 also match.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(7), the semantic-equivalence criteria and the optimization formulation are unchanged. The added period after Equation (6) is punctuation; no mathematical assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: a constrained formulation, a constraint-preserving zeroth-order method, and empirical elicitation of hallucinations through realistic prompt variations. The abstract's wording changes preserve these claims and their scope.

C2.justification: Section 3 retains the same explanations of attack performance, convergence, prompt characteristics and evaluator reliability. Appendix O preserves the limitations concerning scalability, MCQA coverage, targeted attacks and non-reasoning models.

D1.justification: The prompt templates, model versions, hyperparameters, hardware, runtimes and code/data access information are unchanged. The revised randomization sentence summarizes information already present in Appendix G, without adding reproducibility details.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list, Section 4 and Appendix E are unchanged. Introductory rephrasing preserves the same positioning relative to gibberish, trivial and meaning-shift attacks.

P1.justification: The abstract and scattered paragraphs in Sections 1-3.2 receive limited copyediting, clearer instruction-sampling wording and terminology refinements. The arXiv version/date stamp changes, while section order and appendix text remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Revised paragraphs reflow locally on pages 1-6; for example, page 4 places the checker symbol F on the line after LLM. Figures, tables, captions and their placement are preserved, and pages 7-41 render identically.

improvement.justification: v3 provides a limited clarity improvement: Section 2.2 replaces vague wording about injecting randomness and varying content with explicit sampling from predefined instruction components, consistent with Appendix G. Other copyedits improve phrasing. The gain is editorial and modest because the method, evidence and reproducibility material remain unchanged.
